claims.text: Elevated-temperature wear instability in FeNiCrCoCu coatings is driven by a thermally induced sign reversal of intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
The stacking-fault-energy sign reversal shifts deformation from twinning and dislocation glide to diffusive sliding and phase instability.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating on Cu has an fcc crystal structure.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has negative or low intrinsic stacking-fault energy at 300 K.
Low stacking-fault energy at room temperature promotes stable defect accumulation in the coating.
Intrinsic stacking-fault energy is associated with the barrier for an fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Negative or low stacking-fault energy stabilizes stacking faults at low temperature.
Low stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning.
Deformation twins impede dislocation motion and increase work hardening, thereby stabilizing wear.
Magneto-volume coupling and thermal lattice expansion increase intrinsic stacking-fault energy with temperature until it crosses zero.
Positive stacking-fault energy suppresses stable stacking faults and deformation twins.
Increasing temperature lowers the kink-pair-nucleation barrier and facilitates screw-dislocation motion.
A positive stacking-fault energy causes rapid lattice softening and a dislocation avalanche.
Wear resistance declines sharply when temperature exceeds the stacking-fault-energy zero-crossing temperature.
Elastic modulus declines sharply when temperature exceeds the stacking-fault-energy zero-crossing temperature.
Crossing the stacking-fault-energy threshold causes loss of strain-hardening capacity and rapid lattice disorder.
At 300 K, the FeNiCrCoCu coating exhibits stable wear resistance and high elastic modulus because of negative or low stacking-fault energy and stable defect structures.
Calculated intrinsic stacking-fault energy in paramagnetic CoCrFeMnNi crosses from negative to positive at approximately 260 K.
The corresponding zero-crossing temperature has not been measured for the specific FeNiCrCoCu coating.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and baseline fields describe stacking-fault energy as negative or low at 300 K, while the only numerical extrapolation cited places the negative-to-positive crossing at about 260 K. Applying that extrapolation would make the stacking-fault energy positive by 300 K.
The conditions and outcome frame the critical transition as occurring above 300 K, but the stated surrogate threshold from CoCrFeMnNi is approximately 260 K, below the proposed 300 K baseline.
